meta.primaryQuoteRule: Both quotes finite and strictly inside (0,1), with bid <= ask. Midpoint is (bid+ask)/2. Prices and outcomes remain oriented by the original trade-detected jump.
meta.boundarySensitivity: A separate sensitivity permits zero and one quotes while still requiring 0 <= bid <= ask <= 1; these may include one-sided or non-executable quotes.
meta.selection: Apply size, four-times-prior-noise, minimum first-bar volume and endpoint spread filters before greedy six-hour spacing. Follow-up availability does not choose or replace shocks. The paired cohort then requires exact active trade bars and usable quotes at the prior bar, first response, and every displayed follow-up through 60 minutes.
meta.estimand: Conditional trade-close versus midpoint comparison on identical trade-detected shocks, oriented sides and times. Paired differences use the same episodes; this is not a separately midpoint-detected sample.
meta.interval: Approximate 95% Student-t intervals cluster by parent event, suppressed below 20 groups or zero variance. These are exploratory pointwise intervals, without multiplicity correction.
limitations: Minute-close quotes and last trades can occur at different moments within the minute; quote age and executable depth are not observed.
A midpoint is a price-noise sensitivity, not an observed true probability. Trade-triggered selection remains endogenous.
Complete paths and valid-quote screening favor active markets. The underlying 1,000-contract Kalshi sample is selected from a daily-history universe and is mostly sports here.
This does not validate the Polymarket reversal estimate: historical bid and ask quotes are absent from its five-minute archive.
Later news and unverified real-world event timing remain unresolved.
